message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of J.K. Rowling’s best‑selling and widely celebrated books:

| Series / Title | Publication Year(s) | Notes |
|-----------------|---------------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter** (main series) | 1997–2007 | Seven core novels – *Philosopher's Stone*/*Sorcerer's Stone*, *Chamber of Secrets*, *Prisoner of Azkaban*, *Goblet of Fire*, *Order of the Phoenix*, *Half-Blood Prince*, *Deathly Hallows*. These form the cornerstone of her literary fame. |
| **Harry Potter & the Cursed Child** (play/script) | 2016 | A stage play written by Jack Thorne based on an original story co‑written by Rowling. It has been adapted into a film script as well. |
| **Fantastic Beasts & Where to Find Them** (film novelization) | 2016 | Companion book to the “Fantastic Beasts” movie franchise, detailing magical creatures across time. |
| **Quidditch Through the Ages** | 2001 | An encyclopedic guide to Quidditch within the wizarding world, published as part of the “Ivy League Library” collection. |
| **The Tales of Beedle the Bard** | 2008 | Collection of children’s fairy tales used in Hogwarts’ curriculum. |
| **J.K. Rowling’s Short Stories** (various anthologies) | 2009–present | Includes stories such as “The Tale of Tom Riddle,” “A Very Secret Society,” etc., often released through charity or special editions. |

### Other notable works outside the Harry Potter universe:
- **“The Casual Vacancy”** (2012) – Her first adult novel, dealing with social issues in a small English town.  
- **Robert Galbraith novels** (pseudonymous crime fiction): *The Cuckoo’s Calling* (2013), *The Silkworm* (2014), *Career of Evil* (2015), *Lethal White* (2018), *Troubled Blood* (2020). While not authored directly under her name, they’re credited to her pen name and enjoy significant popularity.

These titles collectively showcase Rowling’s range—from whimsical fantasy to mature drama—and remain among the most beloved books worldwide.
